content.title: About
content.content: Hard multigrain pretzels are baked from whole‑grain flour, bran, sunflower and pumpkin seeds, and lightly salted. They feature the classic twisted knot, a crunchy crust, and a mildly sweet, nutty flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The multigrain blend includes at least five different grains and seeds.
The pretzel knot historically symbolized crossed arms, meaning “pray” in medieval Europe.
In the United States soft pretzels are common, but hard versions are popular in Europe and Asia.
The sea‑salt topping helps regulate sodium intake when consumed in moderation.
Pretzels originated in monasteries in the 7th century as a quick snack for monks.

items.title: Rich in dietary fiber
items.content: The multigrain ingredients provide a high amount of fiber that supports healthy digestion.

items.title: Contains healthy fats
items.content: Sunflower and pumpkin seeds add mono‑ and poly‑unsaturated fatty acids beneficial for heart health.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Whole‑grain flour and bran supply thiamine, niacin, and folate, which aid energy metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Magnesium, phosphorus and iron are present, supporting bone health and blood formation.

items.title: Low in added sugar
items.content: Unlike sweet snacks, hard pretzels contain virtually no added sugars.

items.title: Seed allergies
items.content: Sunflower and pumpkin seeds may trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: The salt coating can increase sodium intake, which is a concern for hypertension.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Although not sweet, pretzels are still relatively calorie‑dense due to carbs and fats.

items.title: Choking hazard
items.content: The hard texture can pose a choking risk for young children.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pretzels can be enjoyed as a standalone snack, paired with hummus, cream cheese, or mustard. They are convenient for on‑the‑go eating and can be broken into salad toppings.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For longer shelf life keep them in the refrigerator to maintain crunch and prevent rancidity.
